title: Präsens & Satzbau
concept: Present tense and verb-second word order

learn.heading: Regular verbs: stem + ending
learn.text: Take the infinitive (**machen**), remove **-en** to get the stem (**mach-**), and add the ending that fits the pronoun. Verbs whose stem ends in **-t** or **-d** (arbeiten, finden) add an extra **e** in the du, er/sie/es and ihr forms so you can pronounce them: *du arbeitest, er arbeitet.* German has only one present tense: *Ich lerne Deutsch* means "I learn" and "I am learning".

examples.de: Ich arbeite bei einer Firma in Aachen.
examples.en: I work at a company in Aachen.
We play football at the weekend.

learn.heading: Verbs that change their vowel
learn.text: Some very common verbs change their stem vowel in the **du** and **er/sie/es** forms only: **a → ä** (fahren), **e → i** (sprechen, essen) or **e → ie** (lesen, sehen). All other forms are regular. Your dictionary or the translator in this app marks these verbs. Learn them as a pattern, not one by one.

examples.de: Er fährt jeden Morgen mit dem Bus zur Uni.
examples.en: He takes the bus to university every morning.

learn.heading: Word order: the verb is in position 2
learn.text: In a statement the **conjugated verb is always the second element**. The first element can be the subject or something else (time, place); then the verb still stays second and the subject moves behind it. Words like **und, aber, oder** do not count as a position. Use **gern** after the verb to say what you like doing: *Ich koche gern.*

examples.en: In the morning I drink tea.

examples.de: Ich höre gern Musik, und mein Mitbewohner spielt Gitarre.
examples.en: I like listening to music, and my flatmate plays guitar.

tip: Drill the rule "verb = position 2" by starting the same sentence three ways: Ich spiele heute Fußball. / Heute spiele ich Fußball. / Fußball spiele ich heute. The verb never moves.

exercises.explain: Regular verb with ich: stem lern- + e.
sprechen changes e → i with du: du sprichst.
The stem ends in -t, so er gets an extra e: arbeitet.
lesen changes e → ie with er/sie/es: sie liest.
With wir the verb keeps the infinitive form.

exercises.q: Which form is correct? "Er ___ mit dem Zug nach Köln."
exercises.explain: fahren changes a → ä for er/sie/es: er fährt.

exercises.q: Which sentence has the verb in the right place?
exercises.explain: The conjugated verb must be in position 2; the subject follows it.

exercises.q: How do you say that you like cooking?
exercises.explain: gern comes after the conjugated verb: Ich koche gern.
These adverbs say how often or how willingly you do something.
Time first, verb in position 2, then the subject.
Subject, verb in position 2, then gern, then the object.
Morgens is in position 1, so the verb stays second and ich follows it.

exercises.en: I work in Aachen and my friend plays football.
answer: Ich arbeite in Aachen und mein Freund spielt Fußball
Ich arbeite in Aachen und mein Freund spielt gern Fußball
exercises.explain: ich arbeite, er spielt (-t ending). und does not change the word order.

shadow.de: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag.
shadow.en: I work from Monday to Friday.
At the weekend I sleep in.
My flatmate likes cooking a lot.

shadow.de: Abends lese ich oder ich höre Musik.
shadow.en: In the evening I read or I listen to music.

shadow.de: Im Sommer schwimme ich gern im See.
shadow.en: In summer I like swimming in the lake.
